questions.problem:
What is the value of 
 $f(s)=\operatorname{tan}⁡s\,i+\operatorname{cot}⁡s\,j-\,k$ at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$  into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,i+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,j-k \\  & =1\,i+1\,j-k \\  & =i+j-k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of  $f(s)$ at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$  is $i+j-k.$

questions.problem: What is the value of $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t+1} \\ 1-{t}^{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡t\end{aligned}]$ at $t=0?$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=0$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(0)+1} \\ 1-(0)^{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(0)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1} \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the value of $f(t)$ at $t=0$ is $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: What is the value of $f(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}-3),\,\sqrt{2t},\,{t}^{5}⟩$ at $t=2?$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=2$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{2}-3),\sqrt{2(2)},{2}^{5}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(1),\sqrt{4},{2}^{5}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,32⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of $f(t)$ at $t=2$ is the vector $⟨0,2,32⟩.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Magnitude of a Vector-Valued Function
questions.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨{2}^{0},\,\frac{4}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(1)| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Magnitude of a Vector-Valued Function
questions.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨\sqrt{1+3},\,3\,{e}^{1-1}⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{4},\,3\,{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(1)| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$
